- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to sentiment intensity.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.3) — add 1–3% to forecast to compensate for sentiment-driven underreaction.
- Avoid over-optimistic 30-day forecasts after recent spikes — cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below true peak observed in prior 7–14 days.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Lagged sentiment feedback: if sentiment rises sharply 2–3 days before forecast, adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to account for delayed market reaction.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) — reduce by 1–2% for days 1–5 if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
